NgraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale:
Why these decisions, measured against the current write path, not inherited from comments.
What is fingerprinted. Whole file bytes of spec.xml or plan.xml after the surgical status write. digestProjectFile already SHA-256 hashes on-disk bytes to lowercase hex (src/grace-cursor.ts:1762). A canonicalised parse would be a new grammar that can silently discard whitespace and comments the operator actually saw, which is the class of defect this track refuses. design-context.xml has no status and is not approved. The chicken-egg: hashing before writing approved would make the fingerprint mismatch the moment status lands, and D18's defect is status approved whose fingerprint no longer matches. So the write happens first, then the hash. If the root is already approved, the bytes are not rewritten; the hash is of what is there.
Re-approval. D9 forbids rewriting a Decision. An amended artifact is a new permit of new bytes, so a new Decision. Copying the first fingerprint, the way firstStoredBaseCommit copies baseCommit at ledger.ts:411-415, would pin the spec-stage bytes onto the plan-stage Decision and leave F95 unpaid. baseCommit is a once-ever fact about when the change started. A fingerprint is a claim about what this Decision permitted. Those are different facts and they do not share a reader.
Read-order, measured. F81 said permit lookup is newest-governs at ledger.ts:120. At HEAD that line is a Verdict type member. readPermittingDecision at :848 is any-permit via some(). latestReviewVerdict is the newest-governs reader. firstStoredBaseCommit is first-in-document-order. Detection for this fingerprint is newest-governs per artifact: the latest claim about spec bytes is compared to spec.xml, the latest claim about plan bytes to plan.xml. any-match against every historical fingerprint would let an old matching Decision hide a later junk claim. Grouping by the artifact attribute is required for that newest-governs split; without it the newest Decision in the file would be compared to the wrong bytes. The attribute also makes F95's twins readable without hashing. That reader is this bundle's detector.
Target selection. The skill runs gate approve at spec stage and again at plan stage. Defaulting to the current unapproved artifact, then to the plan if both are approved, pays that path without a required argv token. The measured re-approval (F40 / RM-GITLESS-INTEGRITY) edited an already-approved plan and re-ran the gate; that is the default plan branch. Re-stamping an already-approved spec while a plan exists is the override (argv token artifact). Matching re-approve still appends, so archive/C-BUNDLE-BASE-REF/'s two-permit first-wins tests remain expressible.
Algorithm. SHA-256 lowercase hex, 64 characters, same form WriteEvidence already stores. Well-formed as an attribute value. No algo prefix: a later algorithm change would be a new attribute or a versioned prefix, not this bundle.
Detection home. D18 points at P3.7, which is not shipped. The live precedent is archive/C-CRITERION-CLOSE-EVIDENCE/: a reportable defect that must not break a 0/0 lint bar lives in review, because review findings are not lint issues. F83.1 is why this bundle itself can author AC-CLOSE-LINT as CloseEvidence rather than as an unmapped AC-*. Archives are applied or superseded (47/47); a trigger on status approved is silent there without a grandfather list. The hole D1.4 had to close was applied as the legitimate historical method. That is not this trigger. F108.2 splits the live hole three ways. Row one, no permitting approve Decision at all, is F88 and D18's sequencing case. Row two is a fingerprint that no longer matches. Row three, a Decision carrying no fingerprint, is pre-writer, including this bundle: it has no run-ledger.xml, so requirement 15 will mint an unfingerprinted Decision and the detector stays silent. Apply does not refuse: that would be enforcement, which D18 and F2 already refused.
Applied silence. gate apply is followed by hand-authoring status applied onto the spec and plan, which changes those bytes, so the fingerprint taken at approved stops matching from that moment. That is correct only because detection is silent on applied. A post- archive check that the fingerprint matches the bytes is vacuous or false, not evidence. Widening the trigger to applied would report every archived bundle at once.
Three-way trigger. F108 asked whether the check governs the authoring bundle at its own close and answered split. F108.1 refused the split and proposed a close-time stamp after a fresh lexicon phrase. F108.2 withdraws that stamp: the detector checks that a stamp exists, not that a human ratified, and it only fires if the skippable close review runs. The actual defect was collapsing three situations into one. Row three dissolves the bootstrap. This bundle is never itself stamped. Row three is a permanent legacy escape and is not bounded in time: pre-ship bundle, hand-edited ledger, or mixed-version CLI. AC-REVIEW-DETECTS binds all three rows, including row three's silence on the catalogued error.
F106. missingApplyGateRecord (src/gates/core.ts:507-510) is dead: exported, in the module map, zero call sites in src/ or scripts/. This bundle's detector is a review.* finding, not that export.
approved-contract-drift (src/grace-status.ts:389, hard stop at :316) is git-based derived state today: collectApprovedContractDrift at :654-662 reads trackedChangedFiles. F109 said delete that git reading. F109.1 withdraws the deletion: row three plus no git leaves an unfingerprinted approved artifact, edited uncommitted, watched by nothing. Demote git to a fallback inside classifyApprovedArtifact, a new export from src/gates/ledger.ts. status and review both call it. Per artifact: fingerprint present, compare bytes; else git tracked-changed; else typed absence, never silence that reads as clean. RM-GITLESS-INTEGRITY section 4 objects to two independent implementations (F60), not to one collector with a documented precedence. Keep the state name and the hard-stop message. The state fires on row two, and on git dirt when there is no fingerprint. Row one is not drift. Row three is silent on the catalogued review.* error. No second derived state: a missing record is not a drift, and inventing a name would churn the vocabulary the hard-stop keeps. status and review must not pass different changed-file sets into the classifier; two sets is F60 later. Precedence 1 retires F19's accepted transient by removing its premise: a matching fingerprint is not drift, committed or not, so the false window F19 accepted closes, and the hard-stop disappearance on a matching uncommitted approval is that payoff, not a regression. F109.2: the chain is permanent infrastructure, not a shim. The fallback covers uncommitted edits to unfingerprinted approved artifacts. It leaves open a committed edit to an unfingerprinted approved artifact: silent on both surfaces. That is the original git weakness, unchanged. Retirement, if it ever happens, is a per-project runtime condition: no applying Decision in the operator's corpus lacks a fingerprint. It is not a release milestone. Not this bundle's work.
Hand-authored flow. Today the authority hand-writes approved after a lexicon phrase, then the agent runs gate approve, which records a Decision and does not write status. After this lands, the phrase still gates the operator; the sanctioned write is the gate. Hand-writing and then running the gate still produces a matching record if the bytes were not edited. Hand-writing and never running the gate is the review error. argv token record false stays a dry-run. Skill requirement 15 currently authors F95 by mandating the second run and saying the gate does not set status; that sentence has to move with the writer.
Escape hatch. D1.5 is the analog and is also unshipped. Putting force on the existing approve verb, not a new subcommand, keeps one record path. A forced permit is still a permit so detection accepts it; forced true plus a reason is how a reader tells it from a ratified one. Requirement children still show what was bypassed, so the hatch is not a silent green. Empty reason writes nothing, or the hatch becomes a bare boolean. Force does not resurrect applied or superseded: that is a different transition.
A29.2. D1 said the gate does not set status and a separate verb writes applied. D18 puts the approved write on the approve gate itself. That is a deliberate revision of gate purity for approve only. Apply, archive, and verdict stay evaluate-and-record.

Alternatives.Alternative: Child element holding the digest. Rejected. F81: a non-Requirement child of Decision raises ledger.invalid-decision at grammar.ts:901-910 and ledger.ts:619-622, which would invalidate the event detection keys on. Extra attributes are already accepted.

First-observation-wins, like baseCommit. Rejected. That writer copies the first stored value at ledger.ts:411-415. Doing the same for a fingerprint would stamp spec bytes onto the plan-stage Decision and leave F95 as two still-unorderable records. baseCommit is when the change started; fingerprint is what this permit covered.

Canonicalised parse, or hash excluding the status attribute. Rejected. A new canonical form can discard intent. Detection keys on status approved, so surviving apply by excluding status is not required. Whole-file bytes after the surgical write match the existing digest helper.

Lint change.* error or warning. Rejected. F83.1: a lint diagnostic on this bundle's own approved-without- fingerprint window, or on a 0/0 close criterion, fails the bar on a warning about itself. Review findings are not lint issues.
gate apply refuse on a missing or mismatched fingerprint. Rejected as the detector. That is enforcement. D18 and F2 already refused that posture. Apply stays as it is. Review reports.

Fingerprint spec.xml only, because D18's first sentence names the spec. Rejected. F95 is the plan-stage twin. The named-bundle registry says this bundle pays F95. Spec-only would leave the second Decision still fingerprinting the wrong bytes or none.

Grandfather by absence of any fingerprint-bearing Decision, the D1.4 analog. Rejected as the only trigger. That would also silence row one: an agent that hand-writes approved and never runs the gate has no Decision at all, which is the defect D18 was written for. Row three is narrower: a Decision exists and carries no fingerprint. Archives are not in status approved.

Split writer and detector into two bundles. Rejected. F108.2: the cycle was a trigger defect. Distinguishing never-asked from pre-writer removes the need for a split or a ratifying act. The split left the artifact attribute with no reader and opened a detection window until a later bundle that does not exist.
Grandfather this bundle by change id. Rejected. A grandfather clause for the authoring bundle is the F108 smell. Row three already silences this bundle without naming it.

Close-time stamp after a fresh lexicon phrase (F108.1). Rejected. F108.2: the detector checks that a stamp exists, not that a human ratified, and it only fires if the skippable close review runs. The executor could satisfy the criterion and violate the constraint with nothing machine-visible.

Keep approved-contract-drift's git reading beside the fingerprint detector as two independent implementations. Rejected. F109 / RM-GITLESS-INTEGRITY section 4: two surfaces answering one question from two sources is the C-REPORT-HONESTY defect (F14, F15) and the F60 shape. A single collector with a documented precedence chain is not that. Re-source through classifyApprovedArtifact; keep the name.

Delete the git reading now that fingerprints exist. Rejected. F109.1: combined with row three silence, an unfingerprinted approved artifact edited uncommitted is watched by nothing. Demote git to a fallback inside classifyApprovedArtifact. The chain is permanent infrastructure, not a shim (F109.2). Retirement, if it ever happens, is a per-project runtime condition: no applying Decision in the operator's corpus lacks a fingerprint. It is not a release milestone.

Treat the git fallback as closing the mixed-version or committed-unfingerprinted gap. Rejected. F109.2: the fallback catches uncommitted edits only. A committed edit to an unfingerprinted approved artifact stays silent on both surfaces. That is the original git weakness, unchanged. State what the mitigation covers and what it leaves open.

A second status derived state for never-asked or unfingerprinted Decisions. Rejected. A missing record is not a drift. Collapsing row one onto approved-contract-drift would make the hard-stop message a lie. Inventing a name would churn the vocabulary this bundle keeps. Review is the home for row one; row three is silent on the catalogued review.* error. Typed absence is not a second derived state.

A CloseEvidence command on a self-stamp AC-* evaluated after archive. Rejected. After apply the status is applied and the bytes have changed, so a fingerprint- matches-bytes check is vacuous or false. The detector's trigger is approved; that is the check.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: F88.3 candidate (b): bind the lexicon phrase to the fingerprinted bytes. Not ratified. Would change the attestation format; D18 said so.
D19 / D20 skill sentences (per-step phrase, authority owns the close). Owner: C-APPROVAL-SCOPE.
Co-draft of spec and plan. D18 is a prerequisite; this bundle does not ratify C-CO-DRAFT.
Whether RM-VERIFIED-APPROVAL later makes this fingerprint the local half of a two-party code. Out of this repo-local floor.

Scenarios.Scenario: Spec-stage permit. spec.xml is draft. Operator runs gate approve after a lexicon phrase. The command writes approved, hashes spec.xml, appends a Decision with artifact spec and that fingerprint. plan.xml is untouched.

Plan-stage permit. spec.xml is already approved and matches. plan.xml is draft. The same command writes approved onto plan.xml, hashes it, appends a second Decision with artifact plan. The two Decisions are not byte-identical. F95 paid.

Amended plan re-approval. Both artifacts approved. plan.xml bytes changed. A recorded approve targets plan, appends a new fingerprint, leaves the earlier Decisions in place. Detection reads the newest plan Decision.

Hand-written approved, no gate. Active spec status is approved. No permitting approve Decision at all. Row one. ngrace review with argv token change reports the catalogued error. Lint stays 0/0. gate apply still evaluates as today. status does not emit approved-contract-drift; a missing record is not a drift.

Fingerprint mismatch. Active spec is approved. Newest spec Decision carries a fingerprint that is not SHA-256 of current spec.xml bytes, including after that edit is committed. Row two. Review reports. status emits approved-contract-drift and the hard-stop message at src/grace-status.ts:316 is unchanged.

Forced permit. Unresolved IC-* clarification. argv token force with a non-empty reason. Decision is permit with forced true and that reason; status is written; bytes are fingerprinted; Requirement children still show the missing check. Detection treats it as a matching record if the hash matches.
argv token record false. Evaluate prints. spec.xml bytes unchanged. Ledger unchanged.
Existing archive. status applied, no fingerprint attributes. Lint 0/0. Review without argv token change does not raise the new finding. No grandfather table.

This bundle at ratification. No run-ledger.xml yet. ngrace-plan requirement 15 mints an unfingerprinted approve Decision. Spec and plan are approved. Row three. Review is silent on the catalogued error. If spec.xml or plan.xml is tracked-changed, status emits approved-contract-drift via the git fallback (F109.1). If git is unavailable, status reports not evaluable, not healthy. No close-time stamp. This bundle is never itself stamped.

Matching fingerprint, git dirty. Active spec is approved. Applying spec Decision fingerprint matches current spec.xml bytes, but porcelain still lists the file as tracked-changed (the status write itself). Precedence 1: git is not consulted. status does not emit approved-contract-drift. Review is silent. This is F19's accepted transient retired by removing its premise: the false window between authoring status approved and committing it is closed. The hard-stop disappearance is that payoff, not a regression.

Mixed-version CLI. An older binary writes an unfingerprinted permitting approve Decision after this ships. Row three, not time-bounded (F109.1, F109.2). Uncommitted edit: status fires via git fallback. Committed edit: git is blind; review is silent; that remainder is the original git weakness, unchanged, not this fallback's job. The chain does not close it.

After apply. Spec and plan are hand-authored to applied, which changes the bytes. The approved-era fingerprint no longer matches. Review is silent because the trigger is approved. That silence is required; it is not a skip.
